title: Covariance-Driven Momentum Rectification at Liquid-Vapor Interfaces Near Wetting Transitions
authors: Nelson Bolívar, Gabriel Abellán, Ivaylo Vasilev
abstract: Zero-mean forcing can generate directed transport when a medium responds in a spatially structured way and the relevant symmetries are broken. Liquid-vapor interfaces are a useful setting for this problem because surface-tension gradients, wetting dynamics, vapor exchange, capillary and acoustic waves, electro-ionic screening, thermal noise, and boundary compliance can all carry momentum. We develop a conservative continuum model in which the central object is the covariance between a local response field and a zero-mean tangential drive, $\langle Mf\rangle-\langle M\rangle\langle f\rangle$, embedded in an explicit momentum ledger. In a minimal diffuse-interface realization, this covariance gives the phase-selective drift law $U\proptoε_hΘ\sin\varphi$ for a Marangoni-driven liquid-vapor interface above a structured wall, with exact nulls when the symmetry is restored. Wetting susceptibility then acts as a bounded gain factor: first-order spinodal conditions provide the useful amplification regime, critical wetting saturates because interfacial unbinding removes the short-range drive, and bulk criticality suppresses the channel as the interface disappears. Additional reservoirs - phase change, waves, thermal transport, electro-ionic coupling, compliance, and fluctuations - are treated as compensating channels to be isolated by sign reversals, scaling laws, and budget closure. The result is neither a new microscopic force nor an apparatus-level claim, but a symmetry-constrained accounting scheme for rectified momentum transfer in water-based interfacial systems. Reduced numerical calculations illustrate the phase-selection rules, bounded spinodal gain, momentum-budget closure, transverse chirality, and grid convergence.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive, symmetry-constrained continuum model to explain how zero-mean external forcing can generate net directional motion at liquid-vapor interfaces. It achieves this by rigorously accounting for momentum transfer across multiple interacting physical channels, demonstrating that the rectification strength is dictated by the correlation between local response and the applied drive.
main_problem: The paper investigates how directed transport (momentum rectification) can arise from zero-mean, unbiased external forcing when the physical medium exhibits spatially structured responses and broken symmetries.
main_result: Rectified momentum transfer is governed by a symmetry-constrained accounting scheme based on covariance terms ($\langle Mfangle-\langle Mangle\langle fangle$), showing specific phase selection rules and bounded gain near wetting transitions.
method: The authors develop and apply a conservative continuum model rooted in local momentum conservation, treating the system as a ledger of interacting reservoirs (e.g., thermal, electro-ionic, interface).
model_or_system: The primary physical system is a liquid-vapor interface near wetting transitions, modeled using diffuse-interface methods and coupled to various continuum fields like temperature gradients and wall interactions.
key_observables: Directed drift velocity ($U$), the covariance term ($\langle Mfangle-\langle Mangle\langle fangle$), and the wetting susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Wetting susceptibility, thermal amplitude ($\Theta$), heterogeneity amplitude ($\epsilon_h$), and system criticality (first-order spinodal vs. critical point).
main_assumptions: The result is presented as a diagnostic accounting scheme; the model requires explicitly identifying all compensating momentum channels for validity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase dependence of the drift law, show that chiral patterns are necessary for transverse rectification, and compare gain factors across different wetting critical regimes (spinodal peak vs. saturation).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general principle using momentum conservation accounting, derives the specific drift law via covariance analysis in a diffuse-interface model, analyzes how wetting susceptibility modulates this transport near various critical points, and concludes by summarizing the necessary symmetry constraints for any rectified force.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the rigorous application of momentum balance and the identification of non-equilibrium driving forces via correlation terms ($\langle Mfangle-\langle Mangle\langle fangle$) provides a powerful theoretical framework applicable to open quantum systems where symmetry breaking drives directed current.
